title: The Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY):
summary: Schemes — The Sansad Adarsh Gram Yojana (SAGY):

items: Launched on October 11, 2014, by the Ministry of Rural Development, aims to accelerate rural
development and make villages self-sufficient. Under the scheme, each Member of Parliament (MP)
is tasked with selecting 3 villages (1 by 2016, 2 by 2019, and 5 more by 2024) for comprehensive
development. MPs can choose villages within their constituency (Lok Sabha), state (Rajya Sabha), or
anywhere in India (nominated MPs).
The focus areas include:
o Infrastructure development (roads, sanitation, electricity),
o Health and education improvements,
o Cleanliness and environmental sustainability, and
o Economic empowerment through skill development and entrepreneurship.

Funding is sourced from the MPLADS, CSR contributions, MNREGA, and Gram Panchayat
revenues. Villages with populations of 3,000-5,000 in plains and 1,000-3,000 in hilly areas are
eligible for selection.
The program aims to create model villages with lasting improvements, involving local communities
in their development for greater ownership and sustainability. By 2024, each MP is expected to have
developed 8 smart villages.
